cards.b: c.1905-10: wild, non-natural colour for emotion. Matisse, Derain.
Distorted forms and strong colour to show feeling. Munch's The Scream (1893).
c.1907-14: objects as geometric fragments seen from several viewpoints. Picasso and Braque.
Analytical: muted browns/greys, fragmented. Synthetic (from 1912): simpler, brighter shapes and collage.
Italy, 1909: speed, machines and modern life. Boccioni, Balla.
1916 onwards: reaction to the First World War; anti-art, chance, readymades. Duchamp, Höch.
An ordinary manufactured object chosen and presented as art, e.g. Duchamp's Fountain (1917).
1920s-40s: dreams and the unconscious. Dalí, Magritte, Miró.
1940s-50s New York: large abstract canvases about emotion. Pollock (action painting), Rothko (colour fields).
1950s-60s: popular culture and advertising. Warhol (screen print), Lichtenstein (Ben-Day dots).
Anonymous street artist known for political stencil work.
Known for obsessive dots and mirrored infinity rooms.
Photographer of staged self-portraits: Untitled Film Stills (1977-80).
German design school (1919-33): form follows function; simple geometric design.
Contemporary artist who makes cut-paper silhouettes about race and history.

short.q: Name two features of Pop Art.
short.model: It uses images from popular culture and advertising, and mass-production techniques such as screen printing and repetition.

short.q: Explain how Cubism changed how artists show objects.
short.model: Objects were broken into geometric planes and shown from several viewpoints at once rather than from a single fixed viewpoint.

short.q: Name one contemporary artist or designer linked to your endorsed title and a work by them.
short.model: E.g. Cindy Sherman, Untitled Film Stills (Photography); Antony Gormley, Angel of the North (3D).

short.q: Why did Dada artists use readymades?
short.model: To challenge traditional ideas of art and skill, suggesting that the artist's idea and choice make something art.

short.q: Describe a study you could make inspired by Kusama.
short.model: A pattern of repeated dots at different scales on a coloured ground, then annotated to compare repetition and mood.
